question: A 60-year-old man comes to the physician for the evaluation of nausea over the past week. During this period, he has also had several episodes of non-bloody vomiting. Last month, he was diagnosed with stage II Hodgkin lymphoma and was started on adriamycin, bleomycin, vinblastine, and dacarbazine. His temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse is 95/min, and blood pressure is 105/70 mm Hg. Physical examination shows cervical lymphadenopathy. The liver is palpated 1 to 2 cm below the right costal margin, and the spleen is palpated 2 to 3 cm below the left costal margin. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. The patient is started on an appropriate medication. Two weeks later, he develops headaches and states that his last bowel movement was 4 days ago. The patient was most likely treated with which of the following medications?
